policy: User-approved 2026-09-13: founded_for, site_of_debate, principal_venue. Subject coverage is classification metadata, never a generic publishing edge. No principal_venue claim is admitted without evidence of a sustained role and an explicit editorial selection note.

sources.title: Jack R. Censer, On a Mission: Peter Stearns and the Journal of Social History
sources.note: Publisher abstract read: founding in 1967 and Stearns’s programme for establishing social history’s disciplinary position. Article published online 2017, assigned to the Spring 2018 issue; full text not read.

sources.title: History Workshop: Our History, 1976 journal foundation
sources.note: Institutional account identifies the 1976 founding by movement activists and reproduces the 1975 manifesto’s democratic-history purpose; later feminist subtitle distinguished from original wording.

sources.title: Marc Bloch and Lucien Febvre, À nos lecteurs, Annales d’histoire économique et sociale 1 (1929), 1–2
sources.note: First-page text and bibliography read. Founders introduce the new economic and social history journal and diagnose divisions between historians and researchers of contemporary societies and economies. Only the displayed first page was consulted.

sources.title: Lawrence Stone, The Revival of Narrative: Reflections on a New Old History, Past & Present 85 (1979), 3–24
sources.note: Publisher record verifies author, title, venue, date and pages. DOI 10.1093/past/85.1.3. Full text not read in this journal pass.

sources.title: E. J. Hobsbawm, The Revival of Narrative: Some Comments, Past & Present 86 (1980), 3–8
sources.note: Publisher record verifies named follow-up, author, venue, date and pages. DOI 10.1093/past/86.1.3. This records a readable debate location, not a new interpretation of the full article.

relationships.relationship: Founded in 1967 as an institutional home for the emerging social-history programme Peter Stearns sought to establish within the discipline.
relationships.evidence_note: Censer’s publisher abstract explicitly connects the founding with Stearns’s effort to establish the field’s disciplinary position. This does not date the origin of all social history or assert that the journal founded the entire field.

relationships.relationship: Founded in 1976 by History Workshop activists to advance collaborative, democratic historical work through a journal of socialist historians.
relationships.evidence_note: The movement’s institutional account links the 1976 journal to its democratic-history purpose and 1975 manifesto. Feminist commitments developed further; the later subtitle is not projected unchanged onto 1976.

relationships.relationship: Launched in 1929 to develop economic and social history across the divisions separating historians and researchers of contemporary societies.
relationships.evidence_note: Bloch and Febvre’s first editorial states the interdisciplinary problem motivating the new periodical. The target is the atlas entry that includes this founding project, not a claim that every later Annales approach already existed. This record names the 1929 title rather than assigning its founding date to an unverified modern-title run.

relationships.relationship: Hosted Stone’s 1979 Revival of Narrative essay and Hobsbawm’s 1980 comments, providing a concrete entry into the narrative-versus-structural-explanation controversy.
relationships.evidence_note: Two publisher records identify the opening essay and named follow-up in adjacent issues. The existing revival entry supplies the qualified debate context. The journal hosted the disagreement; it did not endorse one side, and this exchange did not terminate quantitative history.
